sources_considered.why: Primary launch report explicitly describes tool-use improvements and reports Python-enabled AIME results for two models.
Primary experiment compares tool-restricted and tool-enabled puzzle solving and records both successes and failures.
Its tool configuration combines Python and internet access; Heavy also changes inference compute. It is less useful for isolating symbolic execution.
The reported experiments were published after the post, and their timing was not established as falling within the target period.

evidence_items.locator: Section Continuing to scale reinforcement learning; numerical results in What's changed
evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI reports AIME 2025 Python-enabled pass@1 scores of 99.5% for o4-mini and 98.4% for o3, explicitly describing tool-use improvements. These are developer-reported results, and the page cautions against treating tool-enabled scores as unaided-model performance.

evidence_items.publisher: Sheraz Khan, Subha Madhavan and Kannan Natarajan / arXiv
evidence_items.locator: Section 2.2, A Comparative Analysis: The Emergence of a Reasoning Hierarchy
evidence_items.explanation: The experiments report that o4-mini failed nontrivial River Crossing cases without tools but solved cases using Python, including through correction of a failed strategy. The same report records GPT-4o producing an invalid solution with Python at higher complexity, limiting any universal reading.

unresolved_gaps: The records do not establish an average benefit across all generative models and tasks.
The puzzle evidence is a limited case study rather than a large controlled trial.
